title: Grandmother's Heavenly Rice
episode_summary: James Staples and Luke Heslop visit Beheşt in Kensal Green to explore Iranian food, migration, identity and cultural memory. Huri Nuri discusses Iranian migration to the UK, the impact of the 1979 Iranian Revolution, Nowruz, Persian hospitality, tea rituals and the importance of food in maintaining cultural identity within the diaspora. Traditional dishes such as ghormeh sabzi, tahdig, saffron rice and paneer sabzi connect food with memories of family, childhood and home. The episode also explores historical and culinary connections between Iran and South Asia, while Beheşt is presented as a community gathering space and a place for preserving Iranian cultural heritage.
historical_topics: Historical connections between Iran and South Asia
